title: What apo ensembles do and don't know about the bound state
subtitle:
An exploration on 16 apo/holo NMR pairs and 13 transcription factors
Lexi Shewchuk · Rohs Lab · October 2026
notes: In August I had a hypothesis and a pipeline. Today: a new measurement, a method, and a question none of us had asked.
Say the word exploration out loud. Nothing here is a paper; several numbers will still move.
Promise the directions slide at the end — I want proposals, not just questions.
Interruptions welcome, and best, during the two NMR acts.
The project in one slide: a co-crystal is one conformation, specificity is a distribution over sequences.
30 seconds on DeepPBS, 30 on BioEmu. Do not re-teach the pipeline — next slide does that.
This is the August framing, unchanged, so the talk stands alone for anyone who missed it.
BioEmu -> dock to crystal DNA -> minimize -> fnat gate -> featurize -> DeepPBS.
13 pilots, ~90-100 frames each, 12 with full frozen x relaxed grids.
If you were here in August this is the 55 slides you already sat through — ask and I will open any of them.

title: What changed since August
bullets: A new measurement: deposited apo/holo NMR pairs, scored with no model anywhere in the loop
16 pairs analysed, 14 informative, 22 more staged
The augmentation experiment finished — and what it bought is not what we were testing for
One label bug: cost us TBP, bought us NDT80
What this is: an exploration. Three numbers on these slides will still move.
notes: This is a table of contents, not a verdict table. Do not preview conclusions.
The bug is infrastructure working, not a confession — one line and move on.
Flag the soft numbers now so nobody writes them down as settled.
The assumption the whole pipeline rests on: BioEmu is trained on and samples apo.
DeepPBS reads interface geometry. The gap between those two facts is this talk.
We never tested it. That is the question nobody had asked.
The fix we shipped in August: dock apo conformations onto the crystal DNA, then minimize.
The open question it leaves: does a docked free-state conformation actually reconstitute the native interface?
Act 1 answers that with deposited structures only.
fnat = fraction of native protein-DNA contacts recovered. 0.5 is the gate the pipeline already uses.
iRMSD and fnat co-vary at rho = -0.90, so one number suffices for this talk.
Keep it to 30 seconds — the room knows what a contact is.

title: The test: same protein, same bound DNA, three sources of conformation
notes: Solution-NMR structures of the same protein with and without DNA. Dock each state onto the bound DNA. Score fnat.
The holo re-dock is the positive control: it measures what the docking procedure costs when the conformation is already right.
Flag honestly: that control FAILS for 3 of 16 pairs (c-Myb worst, median 0.000), so those pairs are uninterpretable, not negative.
Everything downstream uses the 13 pairs whose control clears the gate.
No BioEmu, no DeepPBS, no training in this measurement.

title: Free-state conformations rebuild most of the interface; generated ensembles do not
caption: 13 pairs whose holo control clears the gate, pooled over states. Switching to mean-of-per-pair-medians moves nothing (0.851 / 0.537 / 0.377); including the 3 failed-control pairs moves apo by 0.08.
notes: Re-docked holo 0.859 and 98% pass · deposited apo 0.553 and 62% · BioEmu 0.381 and 18%.
Row 1 says the dock is not the problem. Row 2 says the gate does not reject free-state conformations as a class.
Row 3 is therefore specific to the generated ensembles.
Say the aggregation clause out loud — it is the number the room will write down.
v4's 0.839 / 0.629 / 0.396 is retired: it reproduces under no aggregation of the saved tables.
End forward: this is a measurement about ensembles AND about proteins. Act 4 is the protein half.

title: The pair set: 16 apo/holo solution-NMR pairs
notes: Mined from the PDB: solution-NMR protein+DNA entries matched to protein-only entries in the same 95% sequence cluster.
Filters: >=10 models both sides, >=84% coverage of the shorter sequence, DNA-binding regulators.
Families: HMG-box, homeodomain, forkhead, HTH, MYB/SANT, ARID, MBD, WRKY, THAP, cold-shock, MarR/winged-helix, Telobox.
Five pairs overlap existing pilots, per the overlaps_existing column of pairs.csv: c09 forkhead/foxa, c02 ETS/ets1, c08 Telobox/trf1, c12 HMG-box/lef1 (also the NHP6A pair), c32 Rel-NFAT/nfat.
Only c09 is in the 16 analysed so far — the other four sit among the 22 staged, which is one reason to run them.
Say once: apo means no nucleic acid in the entry. It does NOT mean vetted — some carry peptides or ligands, or differ in oligomeric state.

title: Why you cannot just use the deposited RMSDs
bullets: Every bundle is a different construct — different disordered ends, different domain boundaries, sometimes a His-tag
A per-entry RMSD therefore lands on a different atom set for every pair, so a histogram of them measures construct length as much as conformation
NHP6A, the same two bundles, two atom sets:
untrimmed intersection — bundles 13.32 Å apart
shared core, 54 of 93 positions — 1.56 Å apart
Separation (between minus within) goes 9.87 Å → 1.05 Å
So: one atom set per pair, fixed before anything is compared
notes: This is the methods slide that earns the rest. Do not cut it.
8.6x shrink, and the untrimmed number is mostly disordered tail.
From trim_sweep_ca.csv, no-trim row vs the 3.0 Å row.
Scope if asked: the sweep covers the original five pairs, not all 16.
v4's 9.47 / 0.81 Å is retired — it appears in no table in the repo.

title: One honest atom set per pair
notes: Four-way sequence intersection, minus expression tags, minus disordered termini trimmed inward while either bundle's spread exceeds 3.0 Å.
Tag removal is not cosmetic: Rok's two members share a C-terminal LEHHHHHH, so the intersection keeps it — pure noise in every RMSD.
Only ends are trimmed. Interior mobile loops stay in — NHP6A keeps a loop reaching ~7 Å.
The core is defined by the two DEPOSITED bundles only. The ensembles are what is being tested and must not define the yardstick.
If one objection lands tonight, let it be this one.

title: Does the pair separate its own states? The gate
notes: A pair earns its place only if the apo-holo separation clears the bundles' own internal heterogeneity.
NMR spread is precision as much as it is dynamics — that is why the gate exists.
14 of 16 pass. TRF1's CI excludes zero and it is still out: 0.17 Å on a 1.1 Å noise floor.
The gate is the RATIO, not the CI. Lowest informative 1.355 (c-Myb), highest gated-out 1.189 (MazE); the script uses 1.25.
Bootstrap unit is states, not state-pairs; self-comparisons are dropped, not scored 0.
The new pairs widen the dynamic range a lot — THAP1 and TrpR separate by 2.7-3.3 Å against ~1 Å for the original three.

title: The coordinate system: a subspace built from deposited states only
notes: Superpose all four members on the shared core, fit the PCA on the DEPOSITED states, project the ensembles in as test data.
Two readouts per structure, both in Å and directly comparable to an RMSD: position on PC1/PC2, and residual — what the subspace cannot reproduce.
Bundle residuals are leave-one-out, so states that defined the space do not score a free zero.
This replaced a classical-MDS embedding that kept only 35-67% of the positive eigenvalue mass. One sentence; it is a credibility beat.
NHP6A: PC1 is 78% of deposited variance, and PC1 IS the apo->holo direction.

title: The subspace validates itself
bullets: For the informative pairs one PC dominates — and it IS the apo→holo direction
NHP6A 78% of deposited variance on PC1 (k = 4 components for 90%)
Dead ringer and THAP1 sharper still — 88% on PC1, k = 2
Gated-out pairs: TRF1 25%, k = 15 · MazE 32%, k = 10 — no direction dominates
The gate and the geometry agree without being told to
notes: Nothing told the PCA about the gate; it is fit on deposited coordinates alone.
Dead ringer and THAP1 are where '% of the way from apo to holo' means the most.
The all-pairs panel (plots/pair_pca_all_ca.png) is a tall vertical stack — unusable at 16:9. Open the file if someone wants it.
Per-pair panels are plots/pair_pca_<pair>_ca.png, all 16 of them.

title: Rok parks at the free state and stays there
notes: Define the two readouts once, here: %across (0 = apo bundle, 100 = holo) and residual ratio (ensemble residual ÷ the bundles' own LOO residual).
Rok: 2% across. The ensemble sits on the free state.
This is the behaviour the three-pair set led me to expect everywhere — next slide is the counterexample.

title: WRKY4 sits essentially at the bound state
notes: WRKY4: 94% across — the case the three-pair set said did not occur.
Same generator, same protocol, opposite outcome.
Hold the contrast with Rok in the room's head; the next slide puts all 14 on one axis.

title: THAP1: the sharpest subspace in the set
notes: 88% of deposited variance on PC1, k = 2 components for 90% — the cleanest apo→holo axis we have.
51% across, so the ensemble sits mid-transition.
But residual ratio 9.1: it also sits far outside the subspace. Position and displacement are separate readings.
This is the pair where '% of the way from apo to holo' means the most.

title: SarA: the most displaced ensemble in the set
notes: Residual ratio 10.2 — the ensemble sits further outside the deposited subspace than any other pair.
25% across, so what position it does have leans apo.
PC1 is only 42% of deposited variance here, which is why position is the weaker reading for this pair.
Four exemplars now: Rok at 2%, SarA at 25%, THAP1 at 51%, WRKY4 at 94%. The next slide puts all 14 on one axis.

title: Position along the apo→holo axis: 2% to 94%, median 55%
notes: BioEmu is NOT systematically apo-biased. Where its ensemble lands varies by system across the entire range.
This supersedes what I would have told you at n = 3: on NHP6A, Rok and VND alone the reading was 'reaches neither basin, never gets to holo'.
At n = 14 that does not survive. Say it cheerfully — it is the best argument for the 22 staged pairs.
Restricting to the 8 pairs whose ensembles stay near the subspace (ratio < 4) changes nothing: median 60%, same range.
Two pairs at the apo end, three at the holo end, nine in between.

title: What does reproduce: the ensembles are wider
notes: In every informative pair the ensemble sits further outside the deposited subspace than the bundles do — 1.9x to 10.2x.
Direction-free and system-independent: this, not an apo bias, is the reproducible signature.
Two readings and I do not know which is right. (a) the generator over-disperses. (b) the deposited bundles under-represent real breadth, because NMR refinement regularizes toward a mean.
Distinguishing them is on the directions slide — this is the one I most want help with.
BioEmu's own paper reports a HOLO preference on cryptic pockets (85% vs 49%); neither that nor an apo bias reproduces here. One sentence — the room will ask.

title: The control: identical input sequence on both sides
notes: Two pairs give BioEmu byte-identical input sequences on the apo and holo sides, so their disagreement is pure sampling noise.
PC1 medians differ by 0.17 and 0.19 Å — 2-3% of the apo->holo axis.
KS cannot separate either pair: p = 0.61 and 0.15, computed in the figure rather than quoted.
Say 'not separable', not 'identical' — VND at 0.15 is the weaker of the two.
So the distance NHP6A and VND still have to travel to reach holo is 13-36x that noise floor.
One real caution: a tag can be dropped from the measurement core but not from the GENERATION. Strip tags from the input sequence, not just the analysis.

title: How much of this is the trimming?
notes: Everything re-run across spread cutoffs 2-5 Å plus a no-trim control.
2.5-4.0 Å is a stable plateau for every pair — the conclusions do not depend on where in that window we sit.
No-trim flips signs, which is the whole argument for having a core at all.
Covers the original five pairs; not regenerated for all 16.

title: And on our own pilots
notes: Same measurement, our 13 pilots, using whatever apo structures exist for them.
BioEmu's best frame out of ~90 falls short of the deposited apo median on 4 of the 5 pilots that have apo entries — clearly on 3.
Be precise about the other two, because the figure is: nfat is a tie (0.500 vs 0.510 on a 10-state bundle), and runx INVERTS.
runx needs care: its best frame beats its NMR bundles (0.250, 0.375) but not its six apo crystals (0.667-0.875).
Either real solution-vs-lattice disagreement or an alignment problem on 1CMO. Keep it in backup; pilot_mechanism.csv is not regenerated.
Not a sampling-efficiency story: the best of ~90 frames does not reach the median of 20-25 deposited states.

title: Apo fnat as a model-free mechanism read-out
bullets: High apo fnat ⇒ the interface is already built in the free state ⇒ conformational selection
Low apo fnat ⇒ it is assembled on binding ⇒ induced fit
One number. No model, no training, no DeepPBS.
Preformed end: c-Myb 0.765 · SarA 0.765 · WRKY4 0.727 · Dead ringer 0.676 · FOXD3 0.667
Induced-fit end: NHP6A 0.194 · VND/NK-2 0.349 · THAP1 0.393 · TrpR 0.406
Agrees with the literature where the literature is clear — TrpR and NHP6A are both documented induced-fit
notes: This is the slide that is about transcription factors rather than about a generator.
It is a hypothesis generator, not a classification — say that.
It is also only the PROTEIN half. The next three slides are the DNA half.
runx stays in backup: pilot_mechanism.csv has not been regenerated.

title: Preformation and conformational change are not the same axis
caption: 13 pairs whose holo control clears the gate. Spearman ρ = −0.18, p = 0.55.
notes: The obvious objection to the previous slide: isn't apo fnat just a proxy for how far the protein moves? No.
THAP1 moves 3.3 Å and still carries only 39% of its contacts. SarA barely moves (0.35 Å) and carries 77%.
But Rok and NHP6A break any monotone reading — similar separations (1.0 Å), fnat 0.47 vs 0.19.
So interface preformation is carrying information an RMSD does not. That is what makes it worth having.
Be honest about power: at n = 13 this is a weak-power null, not a demonstration of independence. The figure says so.
Numbers in data/talk/v5_S22b_fnat_vs_separation.csv.
Conformational selection vs induced fit, the textbook picture.
Both are statements about BOTH partners — which is why the DNA side matters.
Apo fnat reports whether the protein is preformed; MGW fluctuation reports whether the DNA is reshaped.
The lab's own framing: minor groove width reports intrinsic DNA structure; MGW FLUCTUATION reports protein-induced stabilization (Jiang et al., Biophys J 2026).
Nobody has crossed those two axes — protein preformed vs DNA reshaped — on the same systems.
That crossing is a directions-slide item, and the one I would most like to be talked into.
Minimized ensembles keep the crystal's intrinsic MGW profile.
Relaxing the DNA adds fluctuation without moving the mean.
pyCurves throughout (Jinsen's), two axis conventions, 13 pilots.
Keep this descriptive. The correlation with augmentation benefit is the thing we stopped claiming.
Engrailed is the clean exemplar: MGW essentially identical frozen vs relaxed — intrinsic shape held.
MGW-FL is low, so little protein-induced reshaping here.
Read as conformational selection on the DNA side, which is the DNA-half counterpart of the previous read-out.

title: One structure vs an ensemble, on DNA flexibility
caption: Ensemble ÷ AF3 MGW fluctuation, median over 12 pilots: 4.60× frozen-DNA, 4.88× relaxed. Paired t p = 2.9e-3 and 2.2e-4.
notes: AF3 gives one structure and it reads as nearly rigid DNA.
Say MEDIAN, not 'every pilot': the frozen ratio spans 0.89x to 12.33x and exceeds 1 in 10 of 12.
ETS1 (0.90) and TBP (0.89) read marginally LESS fluctuation than AF3. The relaxed ratio exceeds 1 in 12 of 12.
If pressed, name them — the two pilots whose DNA the gate likes best are the two where this effect is absent. Interesting, not awkward.
Reproduces the lab's own Biophys J Fig 3 on our systems — a good place to say the pipeline agrees with something external.
This answers 'why BioEmu and not AF3?' before it is asked.
Baseline vs augmented, paired by seed, differing only in the data directory.
The one design fact that explains everything downstream: EVERY conformation of a protein carries that protein's single experimental PWM.
Flag the shared label here, in one sentence. It is the whole interpretation two slides later.
Across 701 conformations, the spread in predicted PWM agreement across CONFORMATIONS exceeds the spread across independently trained MODELS.
Conformation SD 0.234 vs seed SD 0.149, ratio 1.57, n = 701 baseline states.
Do not pool pilots — that inflates the conformation SD to 0.319 by folding in between-pilot differences.
Exemplars if there is time: EGR1's worst state loses the poly-G signature; TBP's best is indistinguishable from the crystal.

title: What augmentation actually bought
notes: The model became markedly more CONSISTENT across conformations and only slightly more accurate on complexes it had never seen.
Which is exactly what we asked for when we gave every conformation the same label.
Across-conformer SD 0.247 -> 0.202, lower in 10 of 12 pilots, Wilcoxon p = 0.034. HSF1 is the lone exception (0.392 -> 0.518).
Two different quantities: consistency +0.025 [+0.014, +0.036] and accuracy +0.014 [+0.002, +0.026]. CIs overlap — do not claim one is bigger.
v4 called +0.025 an accuracy gain. It is not: that column is agreement with the checkpoint's OWN crystal prediction.

Volunteer the in-sample structure: within-pilot consistency is +0.246 mean. But the inputs are not near-copies — median distance to own crystal is 0.83 of the unrelated-entry distance, and for ERR (1.07) and NFAT (1.34) the states are FURTHER.
So: label-side memorization with structurally distinct inputs.
Unit is the pilot (n = 12). Pilot x seed looks stronger (p = 6.7e-6) but seeds share data — pseudoreplicated.
Close forward: the objective maps every conformation to one motif, so it cannot learn conformational sensitivity by construction. The fix is per-frame labels.

title: What I did to the August mechanism claim
bullets: August: the augmentation effect tracks DNA bend *fluctuation*, not static crystal bend
the committed record is ρ = −0.76 on the relaxed arm, bootstrap CI [−0.96, −0.28], p = 0.006, n = 11
My own stated next steps were: decompose bend-IQR, localize the fluctuation, rebuild from local geometry
I did all three. They do not kill the correlation — they re-specify what it is about
the axis reproduces: ρ = −0.72, p = 0.019 ✓
a complete accumulation of every base-pair step is flat: ρ = +0.07, p = 0.855 ✓
but an independent end-to-end reconstruction tracks it: ρ = −0.62, p = 0.054 ✓
So the quantity is an end-to-end orientation measure, not accumulated local curvature
notes: This replaces the flat 'withdrawn, quantity unidentifiable' line — the re-derivation is better than that.
Say 're-specified', not 'retracted'. The correlation is still there; what changed is what it measures.
v4 quoted ρ = −0.87 and ρ = +0.05. Neither has a surviving script; FINDINGS.md lines 266–267 give −0.76 / −0.53 and my re-derivation gives −0.72. Quote the traceable numbers.
The three figures that follow are new (2026-10-06), built from the retained per-state pyCurves JSON — nothing was re-run.
Caveat to keep: n = 10–12 pilots, and the effect is significant on one arm (p = 0.019) and not the other (p = 0.093).

title: Decomposed: roll and tilt carry it, twist does not
caption: One component varies while the other two are held at their per-step ensemble mean, then the duplex bend is re-accumulated. 10 pilots, frozen ensembles.
notes: Twist contributes almost nothing — 0.2–2.8° of IQR against 10–21° when all three vary (TBP is the high-twist outlier at 2.8°).
Roll and tilt are comparable, and neither alone reproduces the total: they combine roughly in quadrature.
So 'bend fluctuation' is a roll-and-tilt phenomenon. That is worth knowing independently of the augmentation question.
runx is the largest at 20.5° all-varying — and its tilt-only value exceeds its roll-only, unlike most pilots.

title: Localized: the ends are the quietest part of the duplex
caption: Per-step IQR of roll and tilt against normalized position. One line per pilot, median over pilots in dark grey.
notes: Median per-step roll IQR runs ~1.5° at the termini against ~4.5° mid-duplex — the fluctuation is centrally weighted.
That is the punchline: bend_uu is a TERMINAL axis-vector angle, so it reads the quietest segment of the molecule.
It is not a localization failure — the fluctuation is somewhere, just not where the summary looks.
Two pilots spike above 11° mid-duplex in tilt; the rest sit under 6°.

title: Rebuilt: which reconstruction IS bend_uu a summary of?
notes: Left: the August axis reproduces — ρ = −0.72, p = 0.019, n = 10, against the relaxed-arm effect.
Middle: two reconstructions from the SAME local steps. Complete twist-aware accumulation is flat (+0.07, p = 0.855); end-to-end frame orientation tracks the effect (−0.62, p = 0.054).
Right: and only the end-to-end one tracks bend_uu — ρ = +0.85, p = 0.0004, against +0.27, p = 0.39 for the complete accumulation.
Read together: bend_uu is a genuine end-to-end orientation measure. It is NOT a proxy for total accumulated local bending, and that distinction is the whole story.
Panels 2 and 3 plot rank, not degrees, so two quantities on different scales share an axis. Spearman is rank-based, so nothing is lost.
Honest limits: n = 10–12, p = 0.054 is not significance, and the two arms disagree. This re-specifies the claim; it does not establish it.

title: Six directions — argue with me
bullets: 1 · Is the width signature a generator artifact or a deposition artifact? RDC back-calculation on ensemble members? MD on the same construct?
2 · Folded vs unfolded. Some of the fnat gap may be BioEmu correctly sampling a disordered tail. How would you split 'generator is wrong' from 'metric measures foldedness'?
3 · Which families should the next 22 pairs prioritize — breadth across folds, or depth where mechanism is contested?
4 · Cross the protein and DNA axes. Apo fnat × MGW fluctuation on overlapping systems, never plotted against each other. Is that the interesting 2×2?
5 · Per-frame labels for augmentation — whose labels? Self-labelling is cheap but circular; a λ-blend sweep is the cheap test. Better source?
6 · Is 'is the DBD preformed?' a paper on its own? No model, no training, reproduces known induced-fit cases, and at n = 38 it is a survey.
notes: Put it up and stop talking.
This slide stays up through the discussion. Take notes on it directly.
If the room only engages with one, I want it to be 4 — it is the one that needs a biologist rather than a benchmark.
Direction 1 is the one that decides whether the width result is about BioEmu or about the PDB.

a published case with a known right answer; the test is queued
